source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-110: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 110 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the design as a measured hypothesis and separate model behavior from runtime observations. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but do not infer platform facts. Record model and runtime revisions, GPU/NIC/RDMA and PCIe/NUMA topology, memory limits, failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, cache warmness, and tenant policy; unresolved facts are evidence_required. This is Mooncake variant 110.

Define the mechanism precisely: prefill workers create KV blocks and decode workers consume them. Specify block layout and precision, token-position/model/revision cache keys, namespace, placement, replication, leases or epochs, checksums, TTL, eviction priority, admission quotas, and control-plane commit states. Authenticate and authorize before lookup, enforce tenant isolation, and reject stale, partial, corrupt, mismatched, or unauthorized blocks. On miss, RDMA timeout/link failure, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use bounded retry and timeout budgets, recompute locally or fall back to conventional serving, and preserve output correctness. Use idempotent writes, fencing for failed owners, replica health checks, and a rollback gate that disables remote reuse when integrity failures, error rate, or tail latency breaches a predeclared threshold.

Falsifiable hypothesis: under a fixed prompt/concurrency mix and SLO, remote KV reduces TTFT, decode startup, or end-to-end p95/p99 latency and/or raises useful throughput without changing outputs, relative to matched local-KV and conventional distributed-serving baselines. Measure TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, requests/s and tokens/s, KV hit/miss rate, bytes and transfer time, RDMA operations, GPU/memory utilization, queueing, retries, fallback, errors, and p50/p95/p99 with units. Randomize repeated runs after declared warm-up, hold batching/load/cache state constant, report uncertainty, and test output equivalence. Attribute RDMA separately from serialization, PCIe/NUMA copies, prefill, decode, queueing, and control-plane work. Include link utilization, offered load, topology, cache state, and node/link/control-plane failure injection. Confounders include sequence mix, scheduling, replication, compression/precision, competing traffic, and resource contention. Do not claim improvement until the measurements, integrity tests, and rollback/recovery evidence pass.
risks: actual platform topology and RDMA capabilities may differ from assumptions
remote KV may increase tail latency or expose stale, corrupt, or cross-tenant data without validation and fencing
failure-injection and output-equivalence evidence is required before production claims
evidence_required: GPU/NIC/RDMA/NUMA/topology and workload inventory
matched local-KV and conventional-serving baselines with repeated latency and throughput measurements
KV schema/version/checksum, authorization, tenant-isolation, and output-equivalence tests
node/link/control-plane failure injection, bounded fallback, and rollback observations
